messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — serving runtime pod crashloop + node flaps in us-west1. Error spike: OOM/CUDA driver errors. Autoscaler activity: rapid scale up/down detected (3x in 12m).

Alice Nguyen: seeing sustained 502s and token-generation timeouts from the hosted API. Dashboards show latency spikes and a flux in node count. paging oncall now. @SRE Pager please escalate to infra/runtime.

SRE Pager: paging Dave Romero (on-call infra) and Ben Torres (runtime lead) — Pager sent.

Dave Romero: on it. initial triage: kube events show nodes entering NotReady then back, pods OOMKilled + container runtime failing to attach GPU. Probable cause: autoscaler bounce leading to simultaneous pod restarts and NV driver mismatch on new nodes.

Claire Patel: customer-reported failures for embedding and chat endpoints. Saw elevated model inference error rate ~18% for last 8m. Several enterprise customers flagged production alerts.

Ben Torres: joining. quick check — are we still seeing scale-ups?

Alice Nguyen: yes — autoscaler logs:
```
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] scaleUp group=pool-gpu count=8 -> 16 reason=queue_burst
[2026-03-15T14:24:51Z] scaleDown group=pool-gpu count=16 -> 10 reason=scale_idleness
[2026-03-15T14:27:12Z] scaleUp group=pool-gpu count=10 -> 18 reason=queue_burst
```
Rapid changes every ~3-5m.

Ben Torres: that churn will cause driver init races and occasional CUDA allocation failures. mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler, 2) set cooldown to 300s, 3) cordon new nodes to stabilize driver install, 4) restart runtime pods gracefully to pick consistent kernel/driver.

Dave Romero: executing step 1 — pausing autoscaler for pool-gpu. running command:
```bash
kubectl annotate hpa gpu-autoscaler paused=true --overwrite
```
Result: annotation applied.

Alice Nguyen: good. also reducing concurrency and routing some traffic to Dedicated for known large tenants to reduce load on hosted pools. Claire — which customers to move?

Claire Patel: moving enterprise-omega and analytics-inc to dedicated routing, doing a soft failover (no config change for customers, just routing policy).

Ben Torres: I'm draining the newest nodes to let NV drivers finish install on remaining ones. command: 
```bash
kubectl drain node/gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Drained 2 nodes so far.

IncidentBot: NOTE — automatic rollbacks disabled during manual mitigation.

Alice Nguyen: we're still seeing 502s, but error rate trending down from 18% -> 9% after pause and drains. however a small subset of pods still showing CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY in logs: 
```
E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E runtime: failed to allocate kv-cache for model 7b-v2
```

Ben Torres: patching runtime to use conservative pre-allocation for KV cache and disable large-batch optimizations temporarily. Applying config update via configmap and restarting runtime deployment with maxUnavailable=1.

Dave Romero: also noticed cluster autoscaler policy that allows burst above committed capacity — I'm editing to remove burst and set maxSurge=0.

Alice Nguyen: doing customer impact assessment: affected requests are primarily long-generation chat (seq>1024). Short inference and embedding endpoints largely fine. ETA to resolution 20–30m if stabilization continues.

Claire Patel: notifying support and sending targeted status update to affected customers. message draft: 
"We're investigating elevated errors for long-generation chat requests in us-west1. We've applied mitigation steps and are routing high-volume tenants to dedicated capacity. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."

Ben Torres: recommendations to prevent recurrence (to capture in postmortem):
- add a damping window in autoscaler (min-stable=5m)
- enforce driver+AMI bake for new nodes before scheduling GPU jobs
- add KV cache allocation fallback to non-blocking soft-failure
- add a circuit-breaker for burst routing to hosted GPU pool

Dave Romero: I've pushed a temporary CRD change to autoscaler: cooldownSec=300, maxBurst=0. Confirming via logs: scale events suppressed.

Alice Nguyen: reaction :thumbsup: Observability: saved snapshots of pod logs and nv driver logs to /incidents/2468101218/artifacts.

SRE Pager: on-call handoff note: Dave (infra) remains primary for next 30m while runtime rollout is ongoing. Ben (runtime) will keep owning runtime config. Alice remains incident lead and will coordinate customer comms.

Ben Torres: rolling patch applied to runtime, restarting pods with rolling restart. monitoring for new OOMs.

Claire Patel: error rate down to ~3% and latency normalizing. still a few crashloops observed in older node pool — cordoning and scheduling remediation.

Alice Nguyen: deciding to keep autoscaler paused for 1 hour, then re-evaluate. tagging this thread for postmortem follow-up and linking to runbook entry: /runbooks/autoscale-damping.

OnCall-Infra Bot: Scheduled remediation job created: remediation/2468101218 — runs preflight checks and coordinates node bakes.

Alice Nguyen: thanks everyone. final steps: keep monitoring, escalate if >5% error rate reappears or if any major customer reports production outage. I'll draft the incident summary once we are stable. :white_check_mark:

Ben Torres: handing off to Dave for follow-through on autoscaler policy and node bake. Ben out.

Dave Romero: acknowledged. starting a follow-up ticket for permanent autoscale policy change and AMI bake gating.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (provisional) — key mitigations applied, service stable. Update thread with postmortem link when ready.
